title: Strict sections, their complex-valued end and free evaluations
statement: Let $I$ be any small category and $D=(F_\alpha\dashv U_\alpha)$ a dg Quillen diagram [def-coef-dg-quillen-diagram]. A strict section is a family $X_i\in M_i$ with arrows $t_\alpha:F_\alpha X_i\to X_j$, with $t_{1_i}$ the supplied unit isomorphism and $F_\beta(t_\alpha)t_\beta=c_{\alpha,\beta}t_{\alpha\gg\beta}$. Its morphisms are families $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ satisfying $F_\alpha(f_i)t^Y_\alpha=t^X_\alpha f_j$. These form a category with componentwise identity and composition and evaluation $ev_i$. An enriched section end is a complex $H(X,Y)$ with projections to $\underline{Hom}(X_i,Y_i)$ satisfying the arrow compatibility equation and universal for compatible maps from every complex, with the componentwise enriched units and composition and underlying ordinary arrows. A free evaluation is a functor $E_i\dashv ev_i$, with natural object isomorphisms $(E_iA)_j\cong\coprod_{\alpha:i\to j}F_\alpha A$; its transition along $\beta$ sends the $\alpha$-summand through $c_{\alpha,\beta}$ to the $(\alpha\gg\beta)$-summand.
